entity.summary: Vancouver-based centralized cryptocurrency exchange placed under an interim court-appointed receiver in November 2019 after customers reported being unable to access assets and the platform disclosed severe asset and liability shortfalls.
entity.notes: The British Columbia Securities Commission obtained an interim receivership order on November 1, 2019 after complaints that customers could not access their assets. The receiver later reported less than CAD 45,000 in cash and cryptocurrency against management-reported customer liabilities of USD 8-10 million and shut down the trading website. HEI uses insolvency as the bounded primary death reason and does not convert later fraud findings into a separate exchange identity.

events.title: Court-appointed receiver secured Einstein Exchange
events.description: The Supreme Court of British Columbia appointed an interim receiver on November 1, 2019 to preserve Einstein Exchange assets. The receiver secured the premises and subsequently shut down the trading platform website.
events.notes: The event records the operational end and receivership intervention. It does not claim that customer liabilities were repaid or that the later regulatory investigation was resolved at that time.

evidence.title: BCSC acts to protect customers of Einstein Exchange crypto-asset trading platform
evidence.notes: Primary regulator release records the November 1 receivership order, the securing of the premises, customer access complaints, and management's stated plan to shut down because of lack of profit.

evidence.title: Court-appointed receiver of Einstein Exchange concludes its duties
evidence.notes: Primary regulator release states that the receiver shut down the trading website and reported less than CAD 45,000 in assets against management-reported customer liabilities of USD 8-10 million.
